# forumulate_site_manifest (Resource)

A whole site as one document: the `version: 2` manifest of `PUT /orgs/{orgId}/manifest`, the same one `forumulate plan` and `forumulate apply` use. Spaces with their SEO, theme, locales and layout, collections, pages from Markdown, forum categories, sites, domains, webhooks, status monitors, connectors, interface strings and organization settings can all be declared in it.

`terraform plan` runs the API's own dry run and prints the manifest plan's steps (create, update, delete, field by field) as warnings, and a manifest the API would refuse fails the plan on `manifest_json`. `terraform apply` applies it; the apply is idempotent, additive (nothing undeclared is deleted unless `prune`) and stops at the first failing unit, which is kept. A page or setting changed outside Terraform shows as pending changes at the next refresh and is put back by the next apply.

Compose the document with Terraform values: `manifest_json = jsonencode({ version = 2, spaces = [...] })`, or `jsonencode(yamldecode(file("forumulate.yaml")))`. Destroying the resource forgets the manifest; set `destroy_prunes` to delete what it created (see below).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The whole site as one document, planned and applied through the API's own
# manifest dry run. `terraform plan` prints every step the manifest would take.
resource "forumulate_site_manifest" "site" {
  manifest_json = jsonencode({
    version = 2

    spaces = [
      {
        slug       = "docs"
        name       = "Docs"
        type       = "DOCS"
        visibility = "PUBLIC"
        locales    = [{ code = "es", label = "Español" }]
        seo        = { seoTitle = "Acme documentation" }
        redirects  = [{ from = "/start", to = "/docs/getting-started" }]
      },
      { slug = "blog", name = "Blog", type = "BLOG", visibility = "PUBLIC" },
    ]

    pages = [
      {
        space = "docs"
        slug  = "getting-started"
        title = "Getting started"
        body  = "Welcome to **Acme**."
      },
    ]

    sites = [
      { slug = "main", name = "Acme", spaces = ["docs", "blog"] },
    ]

    orgSettings = {
      "search.typo_tolerance" = true
    }
  })

  # Delete what the manifest created and no longer declares.
  prune = true
}

# Or keep the document in YAML beside your Markdown:
#   manifest_json = jsonencode(yamldecode(file("${path.module}/forumulate.yaml")))

# Ids of what it manages, e.g. forumulate_site_manifest.site.ids["spaces/docs"].
output "docs_space_id" {
  value = forumulate_site_manifest.site.ids["spaces/docs"]
}

# DNS records and proxy rules only you can create.
output "manual_steps" {
  value = jsondecode(forumulate_site_manifest.site.manual_json)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `manifest_json` (String) The version-2 manifest, as a JSON document. Top-level keys: `version` (must be 2), `spaces`, `sources`, `domains`, `reader_auth`, `readerAuth`, `consent`, `connectors`, `executor`, `webhooks`, `status_monitors`, `brand`, `pages`, `sites`, `translationOverrides`, `orgSettings`, `prune`. See the site manifest reference for each block. Secrets in the document (a webhook's, a connector's) are sensitive: mark the whole attribute with `sensitive()` if it carries any.

### Optional

- `destroy_prunes` (Boolean) On destroy, apply the manifest with every declared list emptied and `prune: true`, deleting what the manifest created. Off by default: destroying the resource then only stops managing the site.
- `prune` (Boolean) Delete what the manifest itself created earlier and no longer declares (never anything it did not bring under management; only the kinds the document declares). Sent as the document's `prune`. Do not also put `prune` in `manifest_json`.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) How long to wait for an apply, 30 to 3600 seconds. Defaults to 600. The apply is one request that can take minutes (domains, large page sets).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The organization id.
- `ids` (Map of String) The id of each resource the manifest manages, keyed `<unit>/<ref>` such as `spaces/docs` or `sites/main`, from the last plan or apply.
- `last_apply_json` (String) The last apply's steps as JSON: unit, ref, id, action, status and read-back for each.
- `manual_json` (String) Work only you can do, from the last apply, as JSON: the DNS records to create for a new domain (`kind: dns`, `name`, `type`, `value`) and proxy rules.
- `pending` (String) What the API's dry run would do right now: `none`, or counts like `2 create, 1 update`. Read at every refresh, so drift shows here.
- `secrets_json` (String, Sensitive) Secrets the apply minted (a new webhook's signing secret, an executor key), shown by the API once, as sensitive JSON keyed `<unit>/<ref>`. Kept across applies.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# The manifest adopts what is already there: import by organization id, then set
# manifest_json to the document GET /orgs/{orgId}/manifest?export=true answers.
terraform import forumulate_site_manifest.site 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
```
